source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Local-breed and crossbred pigs need less dietary protein than imported European breeds, and the requirement drops as pigs grow: a 10kg local-breed pig needs about 16–18% protein in its diet, a 20kg pig needs about 16% (reducing to 12% by around 35kg), and older pigs need at least 10% protein. The target energy level for all pig classes is 13–15 megajoules per kg of feed on a dry-matter basis.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
